summary: This revision finishes the two-tab sidebar built in revision 1 without moving its structure: the same SidebarTabs strip, rail and Files panel stay where they are. The active tab moves from Sidebar-local state into App state so it can be restored from localStorage and driven by the one shared shortcut registry, while Sidebar keeps an optional local fallback so standalone usage and its existing tests still work. ExplorerPanel gains a context label (app name, Misc or Home) computed in App from the existing explorerRoot result, and an 'active' flag used to save and restore its scroll container's scrollTop when the tab is switched; root selection and useExplorer are untouched, and the Files panel stays mounted after first use so expanded folders and cached listings survive a tab switch. The Projects tab label and the rail's Projects icon show one roll-up dot produced by the existing rollup()/isExecutable/appRollup helpers over all apps. Scale and resource cost: the roll-up is one memoised pass over executable terminals (the same scale as the list already rendered) that only recomputes when apps or terminal states change; header context is memoised on apps/source/appId; no new polling, network calls, commands, permissions, CSP entries, dependencies or storage beyond one small localStorage value read once at startup and written only when the user changes tab; a tab switch triggers no explorer listing, and cached levels stay bounded by the existing MAX_CACHED_LEVELS cap.
